utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, could you call the case number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, case number IT-01-47-T, the Prosecutor versus Enver Hadzihasanovic and Amir Kubura.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Could we have the appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning, Mr. President. Good morning, Counsel. For the Prosecution, Mr. Ekkehard Withopf and case manager, Kimberly Fleming.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. On behalf of General Enver Hadzihasanovic, Edina Residovic, co-counsel; Stephane Bourgon, co-counsel; and Muriel Cauvin, our legal assistant.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. On behalf of Mr. Kubura, Rodney Dixon, Fahrudin Ibrisimovic, and Mr. Mulalic, our legal assistant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I'd like to greet everyone present, Mr. Withopf, the accused, Defence for the accused, everyone else present in the courtroom: The registrar, whose work is exceptional; and the usher, who assists the Chamber with the witnesses; and naturally, I don't want to forget the interpreters. We'll continue with our hearing of the witness. I don't know whether at this stage Mr. Withopf wants us to go into private session before we call the witness into the courtroom. We're in open session. Would it be necessary to go into private session?

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, it appears as if the vast majority or the answers to the vast majority to the Prosecution's questions may have the effect that the identity of the witness could be revealed. Therefore, I would suggest to go in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Registrar, let's go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Registrar. With regard to the issue concerning the scope of the indictment and the element of cruel treatment, the Prosecution claims that digging trenches at a front line constitutes cruel treatment. And according to the Prosecution, explicit reference is made to cruel treatment in the indictment. The Defence made an oral objection to this argument and referred to the indictment, which according to the Defence does not contain a reference to this legal element. The Trial Chamber, after having deliberated during the break, believes that this is a substantial issue and that the Defence should address it by submitting a written motion, and naturally the Prosecution will respond to the motion. Having done so, the Trial Chamber will render its decision with regard to the scope of the indictment with regard to cruel treatment, that is to say with regard to the issue as to whether digging trenches at the front line is referred to explicitly in the indictment and that the accused were aware of this element. It would be good if this could be -- this motion could be submitted to us very rapidly so that the decision can be rendered as soon as possible. So pending our written decision, the Prosecution, if it so desires, may ask questions that concern digging trenches, but naturally if the decision contradicts the position adopted by the Prosecution, all the responses provided by the witness or by future witnesses will naturally -- won't be considered as answers to the questions put to the witness. I can see that Mr. Bourgon wanted to say something. Was there anything you would like to add?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. The Defence would like to thank the Trial Chamber for this decision with regard to the objection raised with regard to the witness's testimony about people digging trenches. According to the Trial Chamber's decision, the Defence will submit its written arguments no later than Monday. Nevertheless, Mr. President, I would like to suggest something: Since the Defence and the Prosecution are more or less in the same position with regard to this dilemma, it's the Prosecution that has to provide proof and we object to it. We suggest that the procedure should be such that both parties could present its arguments by Monday and then the Trial Chamber will be able to take a decision very rapidly and this would avoid any waste of time. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. This suggestion put forward by the Defence would enable us to proceed more rapidly and deal with the problem expeditiously. So by Monday we could receive a motion from the Defence but at the same time the Prosecution could immediately submit a motion to us, and this would allow the Trial Chamber to rule. Because the exchanges, the prior exchanges would have made the positions of both parties clear in advance. And confronting your positions in such a manner would facilitate the debate. The written submission would be useful, because it would clearly define the legal debate and it would refer to the jurisprudence or the Rules followed by this Tribunal with regard to this matter; that is to say, with regard to the scope of the indictment, the scope of the pre-trial brief. And thus, having clarified the issue by both -- having both parties presenting their arguments, we'll be able to rule very quickly. Given the importance of this matter, it would be good if both parties could file written motions, since as I have already said, these are essential issues. Mr. Withopf, I believe that you agree with this idea of filing a motion with us as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: I do agree; the proposal put forward by my learned colleague makes sense. And I share the views of the Defence counsel and the Trial Chamber. We will file a filing by next Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. We're in open session. Would you like to continue in open session or would you like to go into private session, given the questions that you will be asking the witness? But as you know what questions you will be asking, we can't guess what they are - we might be able to guess what the questions are - do you want to remain in open session or go into private session?

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, again I would like to go back into private session, since the answers have the potential to identify the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So we will go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honours, we are in private session [sic].

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true, Mr. ZB, that Bugojno is in the Vrbas valley? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. My colleagues have tried to draw my attention to something which is not really of any importance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At some 18 kilometres from Bugojno there is Gornji Vakuf, that you have mentioned in your testimony; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Down the stream some 12 kilometres from Bugojno there is a place called Donji Vakuf; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. ZB, that as early as 1992 the road via Donji Vakuf towards Travnik and via Komar was occupied by the Serbian forces and that it was not possible to use that road to get to Travnik? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it also correct that at the beginning of 1992 in March and April of that year the Serbian forces attacked Kupres, which is not far from the town of Bugojno?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Kupres was very soon after that occupied by the Serbian forces; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Bugojno from then on was to a large extent isolated from the centres of the republic, Zenica, Sarajevo, and others; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it's not correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a matter of fact, one could no longer use the main roads to reach those centres. One had to use macadam roads via Rostovo and Travnik; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Because of the overall situation, there was mobilisation in Bosnia and Herzegovina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you were already -- you have already told us, you joined the HVO; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that time, in 1992 and beginning of 1993, and especially in 1992, there was a number of Muslims in the HVO; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is. In my unit, there were at least 30 per cent Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that was absolutely normal, because the HVO was much better organised and much better equipped than the Territorial Defence and the army which were being created at a later stage; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your brigade was called the Eugen Kvaternik Brigade; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It had three battalions and several independent units and groups and platoons; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your brigade had between 12 and 13 hundred troops; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In February 1993, the Home Guard Units were also established. These battalions were established, as a matter of fact. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In addition to the Eugen Kvaternik Brigade, in February 1993 the Home Guard Units of the HVO Bugojno were also established; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were Home Guard Units, but I don't know when they were established.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that in mid-1992 a number of Muslims arrived in Bugojno from Donji Vakuf, Jajce, Prozor, and other places from which they had been expelled?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it also true that these refugees who came in large numbers came without any belongings and that this caused problems with accommodation and food supplies in Bugojno? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it also true that in 1992 and especially 1993 a large number of the citizens of Bugojno, both Muslims and Croats, started leaving the town because of the fear of war and the fact that Bugojno was intensely shelled from the Serbian positions? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The majority of the refugees that had arrived in town were Muslims, Bosniaks, and this changed the demographic structure of the town in the light of the fact that the majority of the population of Bugojno started leaving the town.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the summer of 1993, on the eve of the conflicts that you spoke about, some 7.000 local Croats still remained in the town; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe that their numbers were somewhat greater than 7.000.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please move into private session, Your Honour, because I'm going to ask some questions about the position of the witness himself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. Registrar, can we please go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We're in open session. Do we have another witness for today? I'm turning to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, yes, we have a further witness for today. I would suggest to make a short break now to enable my colleagues to come down. And I wish to already announce now that the Prosecution will make an application for protective measures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Mr. President, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. It's ten to 12.00. We'll have a break until twenty past 12.00. We will resume at 12.20 and continue until 1.45. So the hearing is adjourned until 12.20.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll now resume the proceedings, and the Trial Chamber would like to greet the newly arrived representatives of the Prosecution. It seems that a request for protective measures has been made. Mr. Registrar, could we move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 19th day of February, 2004, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.46 p.m.,
